_about: The fixed skeleton of every Onsurity JD, in page order. Same for every role, function and level. 'fixed' text is printed as-is; 'slot' is what the research fills. Counts are hard limits that validate_jd.py enforces. Measured from the SDE I/II/III JDs and generalised so non-engineering roles fit the same frame.

slots.function: Department in Title Case, e.g. Engineering, Marketing, Sales, Operations, Finance, People, Product, Design, Data, Customer Success
slots.city: City in Title Case, e.g. Bengaluru
slots.title: Full role title as it appears on the offer letter, plus the specialisation after a comma: 'Software Development Engineer III, Java', 'Product Marketing Manager, B2B'
slots.lead: 2–3 sentences, 25–45 words. What makes this role this role, at this level.
slots.punchline: 1–2 sentences, 8–22 words. The bar, said plainly.

rules.TRACK: One of: Individual contributor | People manager | Player-coach
rules.EXPERIENCE: '0–2 years', '3–5 years', '6+ years' (en dash, no spaces)
rules.STACK: Engineering roles only. Three items joined by ' · '
rules.TOOLS: Non-engineering roles: three tools joined by ' · '
rules.FOCUS: Roles where the subject matters more than the tools: up to three areas joined by ' · '

slots.lead: 1 sentence, 15–30 words: who we're hiring and why

sixth_key_options.SLOPE: entry levels (0–2 years): rate of learning
sixth_key_options.TEAM: people managers: what their team does without them

your_work.label: YOUR WORK
your_work.group_label_rule: One upper-case verb per group describing a phase of the work. Engineering default: DESIGN, BUILD, RUN, then GROW (entry) or MULTIPLY (mid+). Other functions pick their own phases in the same spirit, e.g. Marketing: PLAN, MAKE, MEASURE, MULTIPLY; Sales: FIND, WIN, GROW ACCOUNTS, MULTIPLY; Operations: SET UP, RUN, FIX, MULTIPLY. The last group is always GROW (entry) or MULTIPLY (mid+), or LEAD for people managers.

the_bar.label: THE BAR

fixed.heading: How we expect you to operate

slots.traits: exactly 5, titles fixed and in this order

fixed_trait_titles: Fast, with a floor under it

ai.label: AI
ai.heading: How we expect you to use AI

slots.lead: Starts with the fixed opener, then one sentence for this level

fixed_opener.engineering: AI-assisted development is the default here, not a novelty.
fixed_opener.other: AI-assisted work is the default here, not a novelty.

minimum.label: MINIMUM
minimum.heading: Minimum qualifications

slots.note: optional, 1–2 sentences in the section-lead style
slots.items: 10–14 items, each opens with a **bold lead phrase**

rules: First item is the experience range, in bold, e.g. **6+ years** of ...
Every tool, skill or spec HR named appears here or in preferred/toolkit
Last two items: education (or equivalent evidence) and communication

toolkit.heading: What you'd work with

slots.rows: 4–8 rows; key is a lower-case category, value is a comma list

rules: Every tool HR named appears in a row

slots.lead: Starts with 'Six dimensions.' then one sentence on what we index on at this level
slots.cards: exactly 6 cards: title 1–4 words, text 14–26 words

not_for_you.label: READ TWICE
not_for_you.heading: This role is probably not for you if

slots.items: 4–6 items, 15–32 words, each 'You ...' + a sentence about how it really is here

not_for_you.fixed_last_item: You're uncomfortable working where a {mistake} can delay someone's hospital admission. That's the seriousness this team runs at.

slots.footer_tag: LEVEL · SPECIALISATION · CITY in upper case, e.g. 'SDE III · JAVA · BENGALURU'

limits._about: Word counts [min, max] per item, and item counts [min, max]. Set from the three SDE JDs with a little headroom. validate_jd.py enforces these.
